name: HIPAA Security Rule
description: Healthcare data protection overlay. Activated by health_records or patient_data declarations. Covers the HIPAA Security Rule (45 CFR Part 164) requirements for electronic protected health information (ePHI).

evidence_requirements: Formal security management process implemented — policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations (164.308(a)(1))
Privacy and Security Officer assigned with defined responsibilities (164.308(a)(2))
Security policies reviewed and updated periodically
Workforce security procedures implemented — authorization, supervision, termination (164.308(a)(3))
Security awareness and training program for all workforce members (164.308(a)(5))
Sanctions policy for workforce members who fail to comply with security policies (164.308(a)(1)(ii)(C))
Risk analysis conducted — accurate and thorough assessment of potential risks and vulnerabilities to ePHI (164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A))
Risk management process implemented to reduce risks to a reasonable and appropriate level (164.308(a)(1)(ii)(B))
Risk analysis updated when environment or operations changes
Periodic technical and non-technical evaluation of security measures in response to environmental or operational changes (164.308(a)(8))
Contingency plan with defined roles and responsibilities for ePHI access during emergency (164.308(a)(7))
Management oversight of security program effectiveness
Inventory of information systems that create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI (164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A) scope)
Asset management process covering all hardware and software handling ePHI
Documentation of ePHI data flows across systems
Business Associate Agreements (BAA) in place with all business associates who create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI (164.308(b))
BAAs include required provisions specifying permitted and required uses and disclosures (164.504(e))
ePHI identified and classified within systems — data classification maintained (164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A))
Retention policy for ePHI documentation (state laws may require longer than 6 years from creation or last effective date)
Media disposal and re-use procedures ensure ePHI not accessible after disposal (164.310(d)(2))
Business associate inventory maintained with contact information and BAA status
Monitoring of business associate compliance with BAA terms
Chain of trust documented for downstream subcontractors handling ePHI
Workforce clearance procedure — authorization process for access to ePHI based on job function (164.308(a)(3)(ii)(B))
Termination procedures include immediate revocation of ePHI access (164.308(a)(3)(ii)(C))
Access rights reviewed when workforce members change roles
Unique user identification assigned to each workforce member and system with ePHI access (164.312(a)(2)(i))
Emergency access procedure for obtaining necessary ePHI during emergency (164.312(a)(2)(ii))
Automatic logoff after period of inactivity (164.312(a)(2)(iii))
Encryption and decryption of ePHI (addressable) (164.312(a)(2)(iv))

threshold_adjustments.reason: HIPAA 164.312(d) mandates person or entity authentication — all access to ePHI must be authenticated

evidence_requirements: Minimum necessary standard applied — access limited to what is reasonably necessary to accomplish intended purpose (164.502(b))
Policies identifying persons or classes of persons who need ePHI access and minimum necessary amount (164.514(d)(2))
Role-based access controls enforce minimum necessary in automated systems

threshold_adjustments.reason: HIPAA 164.502(b) minimum necessary standard — scope violations involving ePHI require strict enforcement

evidence_requirements: Electronic mechanisms to corroborate that ePHI has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner (164.312(c)(1))
Error correction mechanism for ePHI integrity (addressable) (164.312(c)(2))
Data provenance tracked — source and handling history of ePHI documented
Technical security measures to guard against unauthorized access to ePHI transmitted over electronic communications networks (164.312(e)(1))
Encryption of ePHI in transit (addressable) — must encrypt whenever deemed reasonable and appropriate (164.312(e)(2)(ii))
Integrity controls to ensure ePHI is not improperly modified during transmission (164.312(e)(2)(i))

threshold_adjustments.reason: HIPAA 164.312(e) transmission security — ePHI transmitted over networks must be protected from interception

evidence_requirements: Hardware, software, and procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in information systems containing ePHI (164.312(b))
Audit logs include user activity, access events, and security-relevant actions on ePHI
Audit log retention: documentation retained for 6 years from date of creation or last effective date (164.316(b)(2)(i))

threshold_adjustments.reason: HIPAA 164.312(b) audit controls — activity in ePHI systems must be recorded and reviewable

evidence_requirements: Facility access controls to limit physical access to electronic information systems containing ePHI (164.310(a))
Physical access policies — facility security plan, access control and validation, maintenance records (164.310(a)(2))
Physical safeguards for workstations used to access ePHI (164.310(c))
Workstation use policies specify proper functions, manner of use, and physical surroundings (164.310(b))
Workstation security measures to restrict access to authorized users and deter casual unauthorized viewing (164.310(c))
Remote access to ePHI systems requires appropriate safeguards
Hardware and electronic media disposal procedure — ePHI removed before disposal (164.310(d)(2)(i))
Media re-use procedure — ePHI removed from media before it is available for re-use (164.310(d)(2)(ii))
Accountability for hardware and electronic media containing ePHI — movement records maintained (164.310(d)(2)(iii))
Security incident procedures to address suspected or known security incidents (164.308(a)(6))
Identification and response capability for security incidents affecting ePHI
Malicious software protection — protection from and reporting procedures for malicious software (164.308(a)(5)(ii)(B))
Information system activity review — regular review of audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking (164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D))
Log-in monitoring — procedures to monitor log-in attempts and report discrepancies (164.308(a)(5)(ii)(C))
Evaluation to determine extent to which current security policies and procedures meet requirements (164.308(a)(8))
Anomalous access pattern detection — unusual ePHI access volumes, after-hours access, access from unexpected locations
Malicious software protection including detection and containment procedures (164.308(a)(5)(ii)(B))
Password management procedures — creation, change, and safeguarding of passwords (164.308(a)(5)(ii)(D))
Audit log integrity maintained — logs cannot be altered or deleted by unauthorized persons
Vulnerability management for systems containing ePHI — patches applied in timely manner
Penetration testing and security assessments performed as part of risk analysis (164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A))
Security incident response procedures — response and reporting procedures for suspected and known security incidents (164.308(a)(6)(ii))
Incident documentation — actions taken, outcomes, and lessons learned
Workforce trained on incident identification and reporting procedures
Mitigation procedures to document and mitigate harmful effects of security incidents (164.308(a)(6)(ii))
Corrective action process to address root cause of security incidents
Post-incident review to update policies and procedures based on lessons learned
Breach notification rule compliance — breach of unsecured ePHI reported to affected individuals within 60 days of discovery (164.404)
Breach notification to HHS Secretary — breaches affecting 500+ individuals reported to HHS (164.408)
Breach risk assessment — four-factor test to determine if PHI compromise has occurred (164.402)
Contingency plan — data backup, disaster recovery, emergency mode, and testing/revision procedures (164.308(a)(7))
Applications and data criticality analysis — prioritization of ePHI systems for recovery (164.308(a)(7)(ii)(E))
Emergency mode operation plan — procedures for continued ePHI access during emergencies (164.308(a)(7)(ii)(C))
Data backup plan — exact retrievable copy of ePHI created before movement of equipment (164.308(a)(7)(ii)(A))
Disaster recovery plan — procedures to restore lost data and resume operations (164.308(a)(7)(ii)(B))
Backup and recovery procedures tested at defined intervals

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: HIPAA Security Risk Analysis required annually or upon significant environmental changes. No third-party audit required but documentation must be available to HHS on request.
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: HHS Office for Civil Rights (OCR). Breaches affecting 500+ individuals in a state require prominent media notice in addition to individual notification. Annual summary of breaches affecting <500 individuals submitted to HHS.

notes: HIPAA Security Rule requires audit controls, access controls, transmission security, and integrity controls. This overlay tightens baseline thresholds and adds healthcare-specific evidence fields. All 26 AKSI controls mapped to HIPAA Security Rule provisions.
